findings.F1: Over one day, sharp falls bounce back. On the non-overlapping 24-hour grid, the most negative fifth of 24-hour returns (scaled by the past week's hourly volatility) was followed by a next-day excess return of +0.0043 (t 4.33, 3251 cases). The other four fifths all had excess returns between -0.0007 and -0.0019. Fitted on falls alone, the slope of next-day excess return on the scaled 24-hour move is -0.0047 (t -5.00, 7974 cases); on rises alone it is -0.0006 (t -0.75, 8241 cases).
findings.F2: That one-day reversal sits almost entirely in the most volatile third of each coin's days. There the slope is -0.0076 (t -8.17, 5413 cases). In the middle third it is +0.0006 (t 1.02) and in the calmest third +0.0011 (t 2.25). The slope is negative for all six coins (t -1.5 to -3.4) and in 6 of 8 years.
findings.F3: Over 3 days, rises and falls behave in opposite ways. After a 3-day fall, the next 3-day excess return has a slope of -0.104 on the size of the fall (t -3.56, 2669 cases), so deeper falls rebound more. After a 3-day rise the slope is +0.067 (t 2.81, 2865 cases).
findings.F4: How a 3-day rise was built matters, through its path efficiency (net log move divided by the sum of absolute hourly log moves). Higher efficiency was followed by a larger next-3-day excess return (slope 0.059, t 3.43, 2865 cases). The tested top-3-gains share of the rise showed nothing (t -1.24). With the 3-day return held fixed, the signed efficiency keeps a t of 2.51 (5539 cases), while the return itself drops to t -1.56. The per-coin slope is positive in 5 of 6 coins, but each alone has t below 1.5.
findings.F5: Hours starting at 21:00 and 22:00 UTC carry a positive drift. Their mean hourly returns are +0.00055 (t 6.87) and +0.00044 (t 5.76), against a near-zero mean for all other hours. The effect holds in every coin (t 3.0 to 4.6) and in 7 of 8 years (t 1.9 to 5.7); the exception is 2022 (-0.00022, t -1.46).
findings.F6: The tested book lost money while holding a long-only average allocation of 0.10 to 0.19. Its mean daily return was below the coins' in every coin, for example XMR at -0.0017 against +0.0011 and LTC at -0.0013 against +0.0007. It was also negative in 16 of 24 windows.

ideas.idea: When a coin's hourly volatility over the past week is high, the deeper its fall over the past day relative to that volatility, the more it rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy sharp one-day falls in volatile conditions, sized by how deep the fall was against recent volatility, and would refuse to short them.
ideas.name: volatile one-day fall rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall over the past 3 days, the more it rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long after deep 3-day falls, sized by the fall's depth, rather than follow them down.
ideas.name: three-day fall rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin has risen over the past 3 days, the larger that net rise is as a share of the summed absolute hourly moves over those 3 days, the more the coin rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would add to 3-day rises that took a straight path, sized by the path's efficiency, and would refuse to chase rises built through choppy back-and-forth.
ideas.name: efficient rises keep rising
